## Fixes

### Headless runs reported failure on every successful run

A scheduled or unattended run (`coda -p "…"`) exited 1 with *"the turn ended
without a final answer"* even when the turn had succeeded and the report had
been written. An event the run waited for is never forwarded by the session, so
the answer was always empty; the report was still written, which made the
failure look like a model problem rather than a reporting one.

The answer is now read from the transcript after the turn instead.

### A report written mid-turn was judged stale

Freshness compared the report file's modification time against the session's
`updatedAt`, which is stamped when the turn *ends* — after the model writes the
report. The gap is normally sub-second and was absorbed by a one-second fudge,
but a slower turn would exceed it and fail an otherwise good run. The run's
start time is used instead.

### `--deny-ok` did the opposite of its name

The flag means *a denied tool call is not acceptable, so fail the run*. It was
wired backwards: refusals were fatal **by default**, and passing `--deny-ok`
turned the check **off**. So the default failed runs that should have passed,
and the flag did the reverse of what it says.

Refusals are now tolerated by default — the model may have worked around one
successfully — and `--deny-ok` makes a refusal fail the run.

### `--report-path` was never told to the model

It was only used to verify the result afterwards, so an unattended run had no
way to know where to write: the model either guessed a path, risking an
overwrite of an unrelated file, or refused to write anywhere. The destination is
now appended to the prompt.

Each fix carries a regression test, verified to fail against the previous code.
